What Does Gigafactory Means for Elon Musks Tesla Motors

(registration wall)
With investors you would definitely get into lengthy arguments when you will inquire about the over valuation of Tesla Motors (NASDAQ:TSLA) which currently has market capitalization of $32 billion whereas its sales in 2014 was hardly $3.2 billion. No doubt investor will give a number of reasons for this but all of them will be based on future growth plans of the company like Tesla’s ambition to sell 500,000 electric vehicles (EVs) by 2020. In addition growth is anticipated as its Gigafactory will produce enough batteries for 500,000 EVs each year besides producing other energy storage systems.

Over valuation of Tesla Motors (NASDAQ:TSLA) becomes more pronounced when a comparison is made with market players like Ford Motor Company (NYSE:F) with $144 billion sales last year and has $57 billion in market cap. However supporter of Tesla believe that it’s Model S will be able to meet decade end sales target by selling in large numbers competing other luxury cars when Tesla will be able to provide higher capacity batteries and additional interiors luxuries at affordable price.

So no matter what the arguments are in support of Tesla, one thing investors must understand that just completion of Gigafactory might not guarantee the growth targets as similar concepts in other high growth industries have faced the setbacks.

Gigafactory will definitely become the vital element of Tesla’s (NASDAQ:TSLA) growth plan but only when Tesla will be able to generate demand for 500,000 EVs annually by year 2020. When Giga factory will run at full capacity it will manufacture energy storage systems of 35 GWh per year along with assembling 15 GWh additional per annum. And to achieve this target, annual lithium requirement would be 8300 metric tons about 175% more than present level of global lithium production. So the issue is that on paper the future looks very bright but reality would be quite hard.

The arguments from supports of Tesla’s that Gigafactory would generate tremendous growth are quite similar to the ones given in support of industrial biotech firms like Solazyme (NASDAQ:SZYM) which engineers algae to manufacture renewable oil for various applications. Just like Tesla, investors also jacked up its market value based on completion of new production facility. When the facility started operation in early 2014, Solazyme market cap jumped above $1 billion whereas it only generated $106,000 million in 2013. Its annual production was supposed to reach 120,000 MT by 2015 end from 1280 MT in 2014 start. All this looked quite positive as per plan but the issue was where is the demand for such high capacity as a result the company just generated revenues of $60 million in 2014 and now maintains hardly $250 million in market cap.

Even though Tesla under CEO Elon Musk has a different industry to compete but still generating that much demand is a colossal task especially when Tesla is facing higher production costs and delays. Gigafactory will only provide good support in the growth of Tesla Motors (NASDAQ:TSLA) and should not be considered as main engine of growth. So investors must carefully evaluate the Tesla’s strength through analysis of the company’s progress and market demand in next couple of years.
